note: Field values follow WheelView report Table 1 (device_type adds 'unclear', kept out of classification splits per Section 5). Single source of truth for UI, server validation and derivation.
value_aliases_note: Historical values kept in the append-only event log, mapped to the canonical option on read (wvcore.canon). 'lookalike' was renamed 'ambiguous' on 2026-10-28; old events are never rewritten. Prefill keys (lookalike_*) are candidate source categories from data/candidates.csv, not label values.

extra_fields.exclude: one of exclude_reasons or '' (= not excluded); compared between annotators
extra_fields.bbox: JSON list of [x,y,w,h] in 0..1 image coordinates, or []; not compared, kept per annotator
extra_fields._status: 'done' when the annotator has finished the image; only 'done' annotators count towards consensus
extra_fields._status_v11: 'done' when the annotator has finished the v1.1 attribute pass on the image (independent of _status)

note_v11: v1.1 (2026-11-04): fields with "since": "1.1" are labelled in a separate attribute pass (app mode 'Attributes', own done flag _status_v11, own assignments). They never change v1.0 status/consensus/kappa or derived/labels.csv; they are resolved into derived/labels_v11.csv. Every v1.1 field has an explicit 'unknown' (cannot be determined from the photo). Unlabelled (no event) is different from 'unknown'. Definitions: server/schema.json 'definitions' and docs/DATA_DICTIONARY_v1.1.md.

control.joystick: a powered-chair joystick / hand control is visible (usually on an armrest)
control.attendant_control: a rear/attendant joystick or the push handles are being used by a second person to steer the device
control.push_rims: hand rims on the large wheels are visible and are the user's means of propulsion (manual chair, no attendant steering)
control.tiller: handlebar tiller steering of a mobility scooter
control.none_visible: the device's control is not in view or the device has none (e.g. walker, ambiguous look-alike)
control.unknown: cannot be determined from the photo

environment.sidewalk: pedestrian sidewalk / footpath away from the curb edge
environment.curbside: at the curb edge or curb ramp, i.e. the boarding/alighting position next to the roadway
environment.crosswalk_road: in a crosswalk or on the roadway itself
environment.vehicle_interior: inside a car, van, bus or train
environment.ramp_lift: on a vehicle ramp or lift, or a building ramp used for boarding
environment.other_outdoor: any other outdoor place (park, beach, sports court, trail, plain studio background)
environment.unknown: cannot be determined from the photo

environment_from_v10_setting._note: used ONLY as an (unconfirmed) suggestion in the attribute pass; never written as a label

weather.sunny_clear: outdoor, direct sun or clear sky
weather.overcast: outdoor, cloudy / diffuse light, no precipitation visible
weather.rain: rain visible (falling drops, umbrellas in use, rain gear)
weather.snow: falling snow or snow on the ground
weather.night: outdoor at night (weather otherwise not judgeable)
weather.indoor_na: indoor or vehicle interior: weather not applicable
weather.unknown: outdoor but weather cannot be judged (e.g. tight crop)

ground_wet.yes: visibly wet / puddles / snow-slush on the ground
ground_wet.unknown: ground not visible or cannot be judged

size_class.standard: device looks like a typical adult chair width
size_class.wide: device is visibly wider than a typical chair (e.g. bariatric-width or large power base) relative to the user/surroundings
size_class.unknown: cannot be judged (occluded, no reference, not a chair)
size_class._note: a coarse VISUAL judgement only, never a measurement; metric sizes only come from data/measurements.csv

measurement_note: Measured dimensions (height_cm, width_cm, length_cm) live in data/measurements.csv and are only filled from a real source (measurement_sources). Rough estimates (est_*_cm with a low/high range) are written by scripts/size_estimate.py with measurement_source='rough_estimate' into a SEPARATE file and are never copied into the measured columns. Monocular web photos have no metric scale.
